United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $ABC$ be a triangle such that
$$
\left(\cot\frac A2\right)^2
+
\left(2\cot\frac B2\right)^2
+
\left(3\cot\frac C2\right)^2
=
\left(\frac{6s}{7r}\right)^2,
$$
where $s$ and $r$ denote its semiperimeter and its inradius, respectively. Prove that triangle $ABC$ is similar to a triangle $T$ whose side lengths are all positive integers with no common divisors and determine these integers.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Prove that any monic polynomial (a polynomial with leading coefficient $1$) of degree $n$ with real coefficients is the average of two monic polynomials of degree $n$ with $n$ real roots.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $R$ be the set of real numbers. Determine all functions
$$f:R\to R$$
such that
$$f(x^2-y^2)=xf(x)-yf(y)$$
for all pairs of real numbers $x$ and $y$.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $a,b$ be integers greater than $2$. Prove that there exists a positive integer $k$ and a finite sequence
$$n_1,n_2,\ldots,n_k$$
of positive integers such that
$$n_1=a,\qquad n_k=b,$$
and
$$n_in_{i+1}$$
is divisible by
$$n_i+n_{i+1}$$
for each $i$ ($1\le i<k$).

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
I have an $n\times n$ sheet of stamps, from which I’ve been asked to tear out blocks of three adjacent stamps in a single row or column. (I can only tear along the perforations separating adjacent stamps, and each block must come out of the sheet in one piece.) Let $b(n)$ be the smallest number of blocks I can tear out and make it impossible to tear out any more blocks. Prove that there are real constants $c$ and $d$ such that
$$
\frac17n^2-cn
\le
b(n)
\le
\frac15n^2+dn
$$
for all $n>0$.
figure_description: Removing adjacent stamp triplets from a square grid.
